title: A Silver Lining Or A Shovel?
gist: Teaser only: Gavekal says US yields have most likely risen enough to buy Treasuries short term, while many North American investors now see France as uninvestible because of career risk. It names the ECB and European insurers as the likely holders of the bag in a rapidly evolving French debt crisis.

themes.theme: US Treasuries after the yield rise

insights.claim: Gavekal's answer to whether US bond yields have risen enough to buy Treasuries is most likely yes, at least in the short term; it points to separate pieces arguing bonds respond to the Fed rather than inflation.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Gavekal is leaning toward buying Treasuries tactically; the supporting argument sits in other pieces, not this teaser.
insights.quote: answer: most likely “yes”, at least in the short term
insights.locator: In recent meetings with North American clients

insights.claim: North American clients see France as uninvestible, or at least too much career risk for most portfolio managers, because a default or civil disorder would be blamed on managers for missing a widely pre-announced event.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Institutional underweights in French debt may be driven by career risk as much as fundamentals, which can leave French assets structurally under-owned.
insights.locator: In recent meetings with North American clients

insights.claim: Gavekal says the likely holders of the bag in the evolving French debt crisis are the European Central Bank and European insurance companies.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Implies the ECB and European insurers are the marginal absorbers of French debt stress, a channel to watch for contagion.
insights.quote: the European Central Bank and European insurance companies
insights.locator: In recent meetings with North American clients
